November 16, 2026

FAA orders third nationwide ground stop in US history after communications failure

tags: politics, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy, @ericmoutsos

The Federal Aviation Administration halted all departures from US airports on Friday afternoon, citing "extraordinary circumstances" and reasons of safety, in only the third nationwide ground stop after those of September 11, 2001 and January 11, 2023. Officials traced the failure to a communications outage that began during a contractor's upgrade from copper wiring to fiber-optic cable; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said a router replacement in El Dorado, Arkansas caused a Texas router to flood air traffic centers with data, and about 60 similar routers have been disabled. Officials said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. Cancellations reached 17,822 over three days, with roughly 1,924 on Sunday alone, and Duffy said operations should be normal by Monday.

Duffy seeks $50 billion for air traffic overhaul as staffing cuts draw scrutiny

tags: politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich, @oafnation_actual

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy asked Congress for emergency funding to rebuild the air traffic control network, raising the figure from the $30 billion the administration had requested to $50 billion. Critics noted that three different explanations for the outage were given within 24 hours, that a congressional watchdog reported in September there was no reliable cost estimate or master schedule for the overhaul, and that Congress has already appropriated $12.5 billion with phase one running billions over budget. The administration fired hundreds of FAA support staff in 2025, with a court ordering more than 100 reinstated, while the FAA was already short 800 technicians and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has lost roughly a third of its staff. Air traffic controllers interviewed by a reporter disputed the official account, questioning why major system changes would be made on a busy Friday afternoon.

Israeli intelligence warns of Iranian drone plot against Trump and senior officials

tags: politics, defence
sources: @ericmoutsos, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

Israeli outlet Israel Hayom reported that Mossad passed intelligence to the CIA describing an Iranian plot to use explosive-laden drones against President Donald Trump and top US officials, with the warning said to be corroborated by another Western intelligence agency. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller are among officials reported to have moved to secure military bases, and Attorney General Todd Blanche has reportedly lived on a base since early 2026. Trump's public appearances have been curtailed and additional security measures put in place. Some commentators questioned the intelligence, suggesting it could be used to build pressure for renewed war with Iran.

Army officer files whistleblower complaint over drone attack that killed six soldiers

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Army Major Stephen Ramsbottom filed a complaint with Congress alleging that military leaders dismissed his warnings about aerial protection at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait before an Iranian drone attack killed six US service members on March 1. He described the episode as a "tactical failure by the Army, our leadership, and myself," and said he was told "we don't have to worry about protection." The Pentagon declined to comment. Trump separately posted an apparently AI-generated video of troops praying.

Iran strikes US base in Bahrain as tanker sinks in Strait of Hormuz

tags: defence, politics
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Bahrain's military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks on Sunday, its first interceptions since September, and accused Iran of a "systematic hostile approach." Iran's Revolutionary Guards said six drones targeted US radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in response to "hostile US actions"; Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. The Guards also said two oil tankers struck mines on an unauthorized route in the southern Strait of Hormuz and that one supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude sank, a claim that was not independently confirmed and which the US military countered by saying main routes had been cleared of mines. The war, which began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February, has yet to produce a deal, and a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Middle East.

Trump to meet Xi and Putin in first three-way summit

tags: politics, defence
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

The White House confirmed that Trump will join China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for an unprecedented trilateral meeting on Thursday during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. A senior US official said the talks could open nuclear arms discussions among the three countries and that no deals were expected, adding that Trump planned to discuss the war with Iran. New START expired in February, ending limits on the US and Russian arsenals; Pentagon estimates put China's stockpile above 600 warheads against more than 5,000 each for Russia and the United States. Trump said he may also meet Kim Jong-un while in Asia.

Republican senators block Trump judicial nominees as Alito warns of Democratic Congress

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina are blocking judicial nominees from their states, slowing the White House's push to confirm lifetime appointments before Democrats take control of the Senate with an expected 56 seats. Justice Samuel Alito, speaking at a Federalist Society dinner, warned conservative lawyers that a Democratic Congress holds the power of the purse and could effectively cut off funding to the Supreme Court. With a Democratic Senate, few or no judicial nominees are expected to be confirmed over the next two years.

Hegseth says international law should not constrain US military

tags: defence, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said critics should stop quoting laws to "men with swords," arguing that international law should not apply to the United States military. The remarks responded to Secretary of State Marco Rubio's comments on the International Criminal Court and its work holding war criminals accountable. The exchange follows US strikes in Iran that killed more than a hundred people, including children at a girls' school.

Nvidia chief resigns over alleged Chinese spy affair as export controls fight widens

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after news of his affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Treasury, State, Defense and the US Trade Representative had backed export restrictions on Singapore-based Megaspeed for months and blamed the Commerce Department, which holds "the pen," after reporting that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick opposed tighter restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. A Reuters review of more than 150 procurement notices found $3.2 billion in Chinese AI projects built around restricted H100, H200 and H800 processors. Megaspeed said it takes compliance with US export law "extremely seriously."

Senate nears vote on permitting bill that would fast-track pipelines and data centers

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate could hold a final vote this week on BAAJA, a permitting bill co-written by Utah Senator Mike Lee that would speed approvals for gas pipelines, gas power plants and the data centers they supply. The measure would give communities as little as 150 days to challenge a project in court, and tribal leaders and several senators warn it would weaken protections for sacred and cultural sites. Supporters say the bill makes data centers pay their fair share of power costs. Opponents are urging senators to delay the vote until the newly elected Congress is seated in January.

Trump denies responsibility for ground stop as absence draws questions

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @oafnation_actual

Trump erupted at reporters who asked about his whereabouts during the nationwide ground stop, saying he takes no responsibility for more than a million stranded travelers and blaming Biden for airspace problems. Asked whether he was focused on White House construction instead of the aviation system, he said "the White House is flawless" and called the reporter pathetic, adding that he had been holding meetings at the White House during the outage. For more than a day after the ground stop he made no public statement about it, posting on social media about other subjects while his published schedule listed no events.

Mossad chief travels to Washington to press for renewed Iran campaign

tags: defence, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent Mossad chief Roman Goffman to Washington, where he met senior Trump administration officials to press for a resumption of the war against Iran. He was expected to meet envoy Steve Witkoff and CIA Director John Ratcliffe. Vice President Vance was reported to be heading to Camp David.

Record $11.9 billion spent on 2026 US midterms

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

Candidates, parties and outside groups spent $11.9 billion on the 2026 midterms, the most expensive in US history, with $5.45 billion backing Republicans, $5.02 billion backing Democrats and $1.4 billion from independent candidates and issue groups. Spending has climbed steadily since the Supreme Court's 2010 Citizens United ruling lifted limits on independent political spending. At $96.57 per voter, US spending far exceeds other democracies, with Australia next at about $19. AI safety political action committees outspent groups favoring lighter AI rules, $44.4 million to $37.3 million, and California's Proposition 40 billionaire wealth tax, defeated 52.4% to 47.6%, was the year's costliest ballot measure.

Texas Democrats move to roll back Republican policies after election wins

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Democrats have begun introducing legislation to undo Republican policies following their statewide victories, including a bill to end the required display of the Ten Commandments in public schools. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has made a teacher pay raise a priority. Democrats also plan to roll back the state's Confederate Heroes Day, observed each January.

Administration cancels mandated pay raises for Head Start teachers

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration announced over the weekend that it is canceling a rule requiring gradual pay raises for teachers in the Head Start program. The rule was created under the Biden administration. Head Start provides preschool education to more than 700,000 children in underserved communities.

United States skips UN human rights review, a first for any country

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

The United States is set to become the first country to fully skip a UN Human Rights Council review of its rights record since the council began work two decades ago. The council rescheduled the review for Tuesday after Washington missed its November 2025 appointment. The administration withdrew from the council in 2025, accusing it of bias against the United States and Israel, and a State Department spokesperson said it gives "no credibility to the agency." The council reviews all 193 UN member states on a four- to five-year cycle and says a review requires representatives from the country under scrutiny.

United States loses measles elimination status

tags: health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The United States has lost its measles elimination status after continuous local transmission and a resurgence of outbreaks lasting longer than 12 months. Elimination status is withdrawn when uninterrupted domestic transmission persists beyond a year.

Pentagon revives OSS name for special operations oversight

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is reviving the Office of Strategic Services, the World War II spy agency, to oversee special operations. According to a Pentagon release, the renamed office receives under secretary level rank, at least $45 million a year and 100 dedicated billets. The original OSS was the forerunner of the CIA.

Pentagon renames AI office the Super Intelligence Office

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department has redesignated its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office as the Super Intelligence Office. The department said the change does not alter the office's mission, leadership or budget. It follows a September order from Trump replacing the term "artificial intelligence" with "super intelligence" across the federal government.

Microsoft 365 outage disrupts governments and hospitals for a second day

tags: tech, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A global Microsoft 365 outage entered a second day Friday, disrupting Outlook and Teams for governments, hospitals and businesses. Affected users included US House staff, the Los Angeles County Sheriff and NHS hospitals. Microsoft said there was no evidence of malicious activity. The disruption came as the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency operates short-staffed following cuts of about 1,000 employees.

Questions raised over FAA contract awarded to AI firm linked to Duffy's family

tags: politics, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

A Boston-based AI startup, Air Space Intelligence, donated to the congressional campaign of Michael Alfonso in March, and in June the Transportation Department led by Sean Duffy awarded the same company a 12-year contract worth up to $875.9 million to build an air traffic tool called SMART. Alfonso, 26, won a seat in Congress and will be sworn in on January 3; Duffy is his father-in-law. The FAA rolled out the SMART software across 22 air traffic centers on November 10, three days before the nationwide ground stop. The company says its software had nothing to do with the failure.

Alaska elects first Democratic governor since 1998

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won Alaska's governor's race, defeating three Republicans including a candidate backed by Trump. The former state legislator campaigned on household costs and full funding for public schools, and was endorsed by Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski. The result brings Democrats to 30 governorships after midterm gains in states including Georgia and Texas.

Washington teachers union sues to block transgender school sports ban

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Washington's teachers union, the nonprofit TransFamilies and parents of student athletes sued the state to block Initiative 638, which bars transgender girls from competing on girls' school teams, asking King County Superior Court to halt it before it takes effect December 3. The plaintiffs argue that requiring girls to verify their sex to play school sports violates their privacy and breaches state antidiscrimination laws and constitutional guarantees of equal rights and equal access to education. The measure passed November 3 with about 56% support, with backers saying it would make competition fair for girls.

Federal judge orders Iowa to let Satanic Temple hold Capitol event

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Chief District Judge Stephanie M. Rose ruled that Iowa must grant the Satanic Temple's state chapter a permit for a one-day holiday gathering in the Capitol rotunda, giving the state seven days to approve it. The group sued after officials denied its requests, alleging religious discrimination, and the judge found it had a strong chance of winning its free speech claim. State officials argued Krampus costumes could scare children and that prop sticks could serve as weapons; the judge said the props could go through standard security screening, and the attorney general's office said the state plans to appeal.

Spain extends eviction protections and caps some rents after general strike

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

Spain's interim lower chamber passed a housing decree by 35 votes to 34, shielding vulnerable tenants from eviction through 2030 where regional authorities cannot rehouse them, freezing rents above neighborhood benchmarks and barring real estate firms from buying properties below 70% of their value. Lawmakers rejected a second decree that would have allowed tenants to renew leases without a time limit. The conservative Popular Party vowed to repeal the measure if it wins the November 29 election. Protests over rising rents followed the October eviction and death of an 87-year-old Madrid woman, and a nationwide general strike returned the issue to the streets.

Beijing bans ownership and storage of drones citywide

tags: surveillance, politics
sources: @groundnews

Beijing began enforcing a ban on drone ownership and storage on November 15 across its 16,400-square-kilometer municipality, including rural districts, saying the measure safeguards the security of the capital. Residents caught with drones face fines and confiscation, and the rules bar bringing drones or parts into the city; owners had to sell devices or move them outside the municipality before enforcement began. The city halted drone sales in May 2026 and had allowed owners to keep registered devices. Authorities can grant exemptions for uses including policing, disaster response and farming.

Houthi fighters advance along Yemen's southern coast toward Aden

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters that Houthi fighters advanced to Khor Omairh, about 100 kilometers west of Aden. Government forces withdrew Sunday from areas near Bab el-Mandeb to defend Aden and Lahj.

Bomb found and neutralized at Illinois ethanol plant

tags: legal, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Police found a bomb at the Bio-Urja Renewables facility in Peoria, Illinois, prompting evacuations and an ongoing investigation. Authorities, members of Congress and the FBI said the device had been neutralized and that searches continue for other potential explosives. No one was injured and residents in the area remained evacuated.

Dark money behind political creator network draws transparency demands

tags: media, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Chorus, a creator group co-founded by Brian Tyler Cohen and Stuart Perilmuter, is registered as a 501(c)(4) nonprofit, meaning it is not required to disclose donors, and its own participating creators say they do not know who funds it. The group says it has roughly 200 creators, does not publish their names and asks members not to discuss program details, while its stated activities include coordinating messaging. Creator Aaron Parnas said he received $24,000 from the program in early 2025. A sister for-profit firm, Good Influence, appears in Federal Election Commission filings, including a $10,000 social media consulting payment from the Haley Stevens Senate campaign, which received $30.6 million from AIPAC during the 2025-2026 cycle. Critics are calling for legislation requiring creators to disclose paid political content.

Constituents pressed to demand open House Democratic leadership race

tags: politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A campaign is urging voters to call their representatives through the House switchboard and ask for an open, competitive process to choose the next Democratic leader rather than handing Hakeem Jeffries the Speaker's gavel. Jeffries is running unopposed with support from members including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Pramila Jayapal, and has said leadership selection is an internal matter for House members. Supporters of his bid note that Democrats won the national popular vote for the House by 13 points under his leadership. A scripted call template has been circulated for constituents to use.

Airlines accused of price gouging and minimal compensation for stranded travelers

tags: markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Companies were accused of surging prices for travelers stranded across the country during the aviation shutdown, a practice critics said is illegal and warrants accountability. American Airlines drew criticism after a response to a passenger who said the airline provided only $12 in food credit following multi-day cancellations, stating that food and beverage credits are meant to "take a bite out of the cost, not cover the entire menu."

Connecticut to offer first responders up to $25,000 toward home purchases

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Governor Ned Lamont announced that Connecticut will offer first responders up to $25,000 for down payments and closing costs beginning November 16. The First Responders' Time to Own program has no income cap and requires certified firefighters, police officers and emergency medical workers to have lived and worked in the state for at least two years and to buy a home where they serve. State emergency services commissioner Ronnell Higgins said Connecticut needs hundreds of police officers and state troopers and struggles to fill its academies, and a May 2025 comptroller's report found volunteer firefighter ranks had shrunk by more than 62% since 2017.

Marine training center director relieved of command after political speech dispute

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The director of the Tactical Training Exercise Control Group, Colonel Meador, was relieved of command following an incident at a ball where a guest speaker delivered what was described as a political campaign for himself and was confronted by a senior officer. Few other details have been released.

Kentucky county magistrate race decided by coin toss

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Kristen Gifford Fryman won a coin toss for the District 2 magistrate seat in Robertson County, Kentucky after she and Republican Benny Ray Renner each received 91 votes. The state election board recommended the toss, the third such tiebreaker in Kentucky this year. Fryman will join the fiscal court, which sets the county budget and tax rates.

Saudi court sentences Kenyan domestic worker to 100 lashes

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

Three Saudi judges sentenced Esther Wanja Muthoni, a 40-year-old Kenyan domestic worker, to 100 lashes in October after convicting her of sex outside of marriage, basing the punishment on their reading of Islamic law. Police detained her for questioning after a supervisor took her and her newborn to a hospital in August 2025, according to court records. She has spent more than a year trying to return to Kenya with her one-year-old son, and the case has prevented them from leaving.
